governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

findings.description: P3 omits the existing real Chromium xterm round-trip regression, which currently asserts that a returned Agent tab preserves its old viewport instead of scrolling to the bottom; a focused mock contract alone cannot prove the latest rows render after the retained renderer is reattached.
findings.recommendation: Update or add a real Chromium Agent-to-Agent tab-switch regression that uses the activation path and asserts viewportY equals baseY with the latest marker visible while renderer identity and scrollback remain retained.

result.summary: The plan needs a real-browser tab-switch assertion to validate the changed xterm viewport contract.

checklist.description: Make genuine switches to a terminal-backed Agent tab scroll its retained xterm viewport to the bottom after the active renderer is reattached.
Keep the forced scroll out of repeated activation, output delivery, lifecycle redraws, and resizing so deliberate user scrollback remains stable until the user leaves and returns to the tab.

Revise the real Chromium Agent-to-Agent round-trip regression to assert retained renderer identity and scrollback, unchanged baseY, viewportY equal to baseY, and the latest marker visible after returning.
Cover Agent, Plan, Goal, and Standalone profiles in the focused toolbar activation contract so every shared Agent terminal receives the same switch-only behavior.
Update the toolbar intent page to record that reselecting an Agent-family terminal preserves its session and scrollback while presenting the latest output.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P3 replaces the old preserved-viewport Chromium expectation with an activation-path round trip that proves the retained renderer presents the bottom viewport and latest marker.

result.summary: The shared toolbar tab-activation path will move a retained Agent-family terminal viewport to its latest row after the renderer is remounted on an actual tab switch, so returning to an Agent shows the newest text while preserving its terminal instance and scrollback and leaving background output, resizing, and redraw behavior unchanged.

checklist.evidence: activateToolbarTab records a genuine prior-tab change, draws/remounts the selected renderer, then calls scrollToBottom only for the retained Agent-family terminal.

The focused toolbar contract proves output while scrolled up, lifecycle redraw, resize, and repeated activation leave forcedScrolls at 0; leaving and returning increments it exactly once and resumes bottom-following.

The real Chromium Agent-to-Agent round trip uses the production activation path and asserts retained xterm identities and scrollback, unchanged baseY, viewportY equal to baseY, and FIRST-LATEST-MARKER visible after return.
The focused switch-only contract loops over Agent, Plan, Goal, and Standalone profiles and verifies identical scroll behavior for each.
docs/intent/04-surfaces/03-browser/15-toolbar.md now states that returning to Agent-family terminals preserves session and scrollback while presenting latest output at the bottom.
